{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our fish was built and connected, and the start domino was traced by eye to knock over about 123 of the 125 standing dominoes. I contributed the stretch that carried the fall from the end of the belly line out to the tail. I sketched it on the pad at the 4:45 mark and laid it over several builds from 5:00 to 6:30. This stretch is what linked the lower body to the rest of the run, so the push could travel round the whole fish.

Execution: I started with close inspections of the joints early on, at 1:30, 2:00, 2:45 and 4:00, so I knew where the run was solid before I added to it. I then sketched my stroke starting from the end of an existing line, as the table agreed, and traced it from the pad. Afterward I inspected the join twice, at 6:45 and 7:00, and then kept my hands off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout. I confirmed who had which stroke, asked Maya to stop at a clear point so my stretch could catch on, and asked Tom to check the joint where our lines met. I stayed clear of the head and nose while Leo worked there, and I stayed off the final nudges at the upper tail join. I also encouraged people and kept the mood light.

Leadership: I helped the table commit quickly to the fish, and I split the remaining work by pointing out the open stretch near the end of the belly and taking it myself. I gave regular status updates, such as which parts were connected and dark from the start. I also called for hands off before the push so the finished work stayed intact.", "my_share_percent": 30}
